messages:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: SEV-2 alert — increased 5xxs from inference pool in az1a, elevated latency and TCP retransmits showing up on netplane. Auto-escalating to #incidents and paging oncall.

Alex B: @here seeing large cluster of `ECONNRESET` and `kvcache stall` errors from gpt-medium replicas in az1a. Latency p50 -> 230ms, p95 -> 1.8s. Request rate steady.

Priya K: Confirmed. Graphs: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/xyz/inference-latency?orgId=1&var-az=az1a -> sudden rise at 10:03 UTC, correlates with host-level network errors.

Eli (oncall): I'm on it. Paging infra-sre runbook. First step: isolate whether this is EC2 instance network saturation, ENI/eni-attach rate limiting, or AZ-level network plane issue.

Marina L: Customer reports for tiered hosted API: 12 customers seeing timeouts, some increased retries. Support Ops is collecting request_ids. @Support Ops can you paste an example trace?

Support Ops: here's sample trace id 3f2a7c — client sees 504 after 30s. Upstream logs show repeated RST from backend within KV-cache fetch.

Alex B: Running `ssh` into a few affected hosts shows high softirq and tx drops. NIC stats: ```rx_errors: 0
tx_errors: 1200
tx_dropped: 1100
tx_queue_length: 4096
interrupts: high
ethtool -S eth0 | grep tx:    tx_packets: 123456
``` So likely host NIC queuing/backpressure.

Eli (oncall): Good. Let's move to active mitigations: 1) Reduce inbound load to az1a by updating routing policy to favor eu-west-2 and us-west-2 for new requests. 2) Kick off gradual drain of the worst hosts. 3) Lower DNS TTL for inference endpoints to speed reroute. 4) If capacity insufficient, fall back to smaller model variant for non-SLA customers.

Priya K: I'm updating routing policy now to adjust weight: az1a -> 20%, us-west-2 -> +30%, eu-west-2 -> +50%. Patch applied to traffic-router: `trafficctl set-weight az1a 20 --commit`

Deploy Bot: rollout started for traffic-router config (change id: tr-2026-az-route-7). Canary to 5% for 60s then ramp.

Alex B: Updating DNS TTL for inference.redwood.ai from 60 -> 15 to accelerate client-side reconnection. Doing via Route53 change.

Marina L: Support Ops — message to affected customers: short status update ready? We should call out mitigation and recommended client backoff.

Support Ops: Drafting now: "We're seeing networking degradation in AWS az1a impacting inference latency/reliability. We've initiated automated rerouting and are actively draining affected hosts. Some requests may be retried or served from alternate regions. We'll post updates — incident ref: INC-2067001234."

Eli (oncall): Begin host drains: `node-drain --filter 'az=az1a and nic_errors>100' --batch 5` — avoid removing too many replicas at once. Also enabling temporary autoscale on dedicated pools in us-west-2.

Alex B: Drains show in progress. One host failed to gracefully drain due to stuck kvcache handles. Stack trace snippet in logs: ```ERROR SyncKV: timeout waiting for shard lock after 45s
  at kvcache/lock.go:142
  at inference/serve.go:88
```

Priya K: Opening quick patch to bump kvcache eviction threshold on drained nodes to force eviction: `KVCACHE_EVICT_TIMEOUT=5s` set via instance user-data override for drain batch. Rolling now.

Incident Bot: Pager duty acknowledgement by Eli (oncall) at 10:08 UTC.

Marina L: Monitoring customer-queries channel — a few customers asked about data integrity. Confirming: no model weights changed, no storage errors. Only network/connectivity inducing retries.

Eli (oncall): Any signs of ENI attach throttles or control plane errors? Alex, can you grep cloudtrail?

Alex B: CloudTrail shows a burst of API rate limits around 10:02 for `AttachNetworkInterface` in az1a region from internal autoscaling jobs — but not massive. I think primary is host NIC TX backpressure + potential upstream AZ network fabric requeueing.

Priya K: If the AZ network plane is misbehaving we should consider cross-region failover for critical control-plane traffic (KV sync, heartbeat). Opening runbook step to set control-plane pref to eu-west-2: `controlplane set-preferred-region eu-west-2`

Support Ops: Sent customer update v1.0 to 12 affected accounts. One enterprise asked for ETA — replying with currently estimating partial recovery in 20-40 minutes depending on drain success.

Deploy Bot: traffic-router canary passed 60s. ramping to 50% over next 2 minutes.

Alex B: After reroute, p99 latency drops from 3.2s -> 650ms for global traffic; az1a still has degraded tails for in-az traffic, but overall throughput stable.

Eli (oncall): Continue drains until kube pods on host show 0 running for the worst 15 hosts. Keep an eye on autoscale in us-west-2 — make sure we don't overshoot commit limits.

Priya K: KVCACHE eviction override seems to have helped on 9/15 drained hosts — they released connections and drained cleanly.

Marina L: Support Ops: customers acknowledging update. Ops asked about credits/compensation? Hold that to post-incident review.

Eli (oncall): Post-mitigation checklist: 1) Confirm all critical hosts drained or healthy 2) Revert routing weights once az stable 3) Increase monitoring alert thresholds to catch similar soft-nic errors 4) Open infra ticket with AWS for packet drop investigation and NIC firmware / instance type checks.

Alex B: Creating infra ticket with AWS (case: 987654321) including PCAPs and NIC stats. Also adding host list and time windows.

Incident Bot: Incident severity reduced to SEV-3 at 10:32 UTC — customer impact mitigated, ongoing investigation with AWS.

Eli (oncall): Thanks team. I'll hand off to Marina for customer comms and Alex for AWS follow-up. Pls add any lingering actions to the incident doc.

Marina L: Taking postmortem lead. Starting incident document: https://confluence.redwood.internal/x/az1a-netplane-backpressure-2067001234

Support Ops: Closing live thread for customers. Will post final update when incident doc ready. :white_check_mark:
